mcq.q: Transpiration from the leaves is important because it
choices: B Pulls water and nutrients up the vine and cools the canopy
mcq.answer: B Pulls water and nutrients up the vine and cools the canopy
mcq.why: Water lost at the stomata draws the transpiration stream; excess heat or drought shuts stomata.

mcq.q: A cool climate is defined in WSET teaching mainly by
choices: B Growing-season heat that is just enough to ripen early varieties
D A ban on red grapes
mcq.answer: B Growing-season heat that is just enough to ripen early varieties
mcq.why: Heat summation / growing-season temperature bands: cool, moderate, warm, hot.

mcq.q: Powdery mildew (oidium) thrives in
choices: B Shady, moderately humid canopies and is controlled with sulphur
mcq.answer: B Shady, moderately humid canopies and is controlled with sulphur
mcq.why: It does not need free water on the leaf; a dense canopy is a risk.

mcq.q: Irrigation in a dry region is used to
choices: A Always maximise yield with no thought for quality
B Avoid severe water stress so ripening can finish
C Replace the need for any canopy work
mcq.answer: B Avoid severe water stress so ripening can finish
mcq.why: Regulated deficit irrigation can even improve quality; drought shutdown stops ripening.

mcq.q: Extended post-ferment maceration on red skins is intended to
choices: A Strip all tannin before pressing
B Polymerise and integrate tannin and colour for a more stable wine
C Keep banana notes from carbonic maceration
mcq.answer: B Polymerise and integrate tannin and colour for a more stable wine
mcq.why: Time on skins after dryness can soften the tannin feel if seeds are ripe.

mcq.q: The main antimicrobial role of SO2 in must is to
choices: B Inhibit unwanted yeasts and bacteria before a chosen ferment
mcq.answer: B Inhibit unwanted yeasts and bacteria before a chosen ferment
mcq.why: A modest addition lets the desired yeast dominate; it also limits browning.

mcq.q: A stuck alcoholic fermentation has
choices: A Finished dry with no sugar
B Stopped while fermentable sugar remains, risking spoilage
mcq.answer: B Stopped while fermentable sugar remains, risking spoilage
mcq.why: Low nutrients, excess cold/heat or very high sugar can stall yeast.

mcq.q: Concrete or large oak vats are often preferred to small new barriques when the aim is
choices: B A slower, gentler oxygen exchange without dominant wood flavour
C A sealed, totally inert ferment like a can
mcq.answer: B A slower, gentler oxygen exchange without dominant wood flavour
mcq.why: Mass and shape buffer temperature; oxygen is modest; fruit stays in front.

mcq.q: Pauillac is associated with
choices: B A high density of Médoc first-growth Cabernet estates
mcq.answer: B A high density of Médoc first-growth Cabernet estates
mcq.why: Lafite, Latour and Mouton sit in Pauillac; firm, cedar-and-cassis stereotype.

mcq.q: Cérons and Monbazillac are
choices: B Sweet white appellations (Graves and South-West) in the Sauternes mould
mcq.answer: B Sweet white appellations (Graves and South-West) in the Sauternes mould
mcq.why: Botrytis whites; Monbazillac is Bergerac, not Bordeaux, but the style is cousin.

mcq.q: Nuits-Saint-Georges is a
choices: A Côte de Beaune white village with no reds
B Côte de Nuits red village (no Grand Cru of its own in the village name)
mcq.answer: B Côte de Nuits red village (no Grand Cru of its own in the village name)
mcq.why: Important Côte de Nuits commune; Premiers Crus, sturdy Pinot.

mcq.q: Saint-Véran and Viré-Clessé are
mcq.answer: A Mâconnais Chardonnay AOCs
mcq.why: Named Mâconnais whites above generic Mâcon-Villages.

mcq.q: Menetou-Salon, Quincy and Reuilly are
choices: B Central Loire Sauvignon Blanc appellations near Sancerre
mcq.answer: B Central Loire Sauvignon Blanc appellations near Sancerre
mcq.why: Cheaper neighbours of Sancerre/Pouilly-Fumé; same grape.

mcq.q: Coteaux du Layon is known for
choices: B Sweet Chenin Blanc, often with noble rot
mcq.answer: B Sweet Chenin Blanc, often with noble rot
mcq.why: The Layon valley’s autumn mists; Quarts de Chaume and Bonnezeaux sit within it.

mcq.q: Château-Grillet is
choices: A A large Côtes du Rhône village
B A tiny Viognier AOC enclosed by Condrieu
C A southern GSM estate name with no AOC
mcq.answer: B A tiny Viognier AOC enclosed by Condrieu
mcq.why: One of France’s smallest AOCs; 100% Viognier.

mcq.q: Vacqueyras, like Gigondas, produces
choices: B Grenache-based reds (and some white/rosé) in the Southern Rhône
mcq.answer: B Grenache-based reds (and some white/rosé) in the Southern Rhône
mcq.why: Cairanne and others have joined this mid-tier of named southern villages.

mcq.q: Bandol red is based on
choices: B Mourvèdre, from Provence’s warm, coastal terraces
mcq.answer: B Mourvèdre, from Provence’s warm, coastal terraces
mcq.why: Mourvèdre needs heat; Bandol is Provence’s age-worthy red (and a serious rosé).

mcq.q: Alsace Pinot Noir is typically
choices: A As full and tannic as Napa Cabernet
B A light to medium red (or rosé), the region’s only black grape of note
C A Grand Cru sweet wine by default
mcq.answer: B A light to medium red (or rosé), the region’s only black grape of note
mcq.why: Warmer sites and better work have deepened some examples, but it remains a minority.

mcq.q: Gattinara and Ghemme are
choices: B Alto Piemonte Nebbiolo (Spanna) wines, usually lighter than Barolo
mcq.answer: B Alto Piemonte Nebbiolo (Spanna) wines, usually lighter than Barolo
mcq.why: Cooler, higher, often with a little local blending grapes; volcanic/alpine soils.

mcq.q: Morellino di Scansano is a
choices: B Maremma Sangiovese from warmer coastal Tuscany
mcq.answer: B Maremma Sangiovese from warmer coastal Tuscany
mcq.why: Earlier-drinking, riper Sangiovese than high Chianti Classico.

mcq.q: Lugana is a dry white from
choices: A The Veneto/Lombardy shores of Garda, from Turbiana (a Trebbiano relation)
mcq.answer: A The Veneto/Lombardy shores of Garda, from Turbiana (a Trebbiano relation)
mcq.why: Garda’s fuller, often lees-aged white; not Pinot Grigio by default.

mcq.q: Etna Bianco is typically based on
choices: B Carricante, from high volcanic slopes
mcq.answer: B Carricante, from high volcanic slopes
mcq.why: High acid, citrus and herb; Etna Rosso is Nerello Mascalese.

mcq.q: Jumilla and Yecla in south-east Spain are associated with
choices: B Monastrell (Mourvèdre) in a hot, dry climate
mcq.answer: B Monastrell (Mourvèdre) in a hot, dry climate
mcq.why: Bush vines, altitude in places, ripe, often inexpensive reds.

mcq.q: Rías Baixas sub-zones such as Val do Salnés are important because
choices: A They are all inland desert
B Cooler coastal sites shape the most classic Albariño
mcq.answer: B Cooler coastal sites shape the most classic Albariño
mcq.why: Salnés is the original, coolest core; Condado and others are a little warmer.

mcq.q: Cava’s still-wine cousins in Penedès also grow
choices: B International and local varieties for still wines as well as sparkling base
mcq.answer: B International and local varieties for still wines as well as sparkling base
mcq.why: Penedès is a still-wine region too; do not confuse still Penedès with DO Cava.

mcq.q: Rheinhessen, once seen only as a bulk source, now also produces
choices: B Serious dry Riesling from sites such as the Roter Hang
mcq.answer: B Serious dry Riesling from sites such as the Roter Hang
mcq.why: Germany’s largest region; quality has risen, especially dry Riesling and some Pinot.

mcq.q: Wachau Smaragd on a label indicates
choices: A The lightest, earliest wine of the valley
B A ripe, fuller category of still wine (often Riesling or Grüner)
mcq.answer: B A ripe, fuller category of still wine (often Riesling or Grüner)
mcq.why: Steinfeder / Federspiel / Smaragd is the Vinea Wachau ripeness ladder.

mcq.q: Trás-os-Montes and Lisboa are Portuguese regions that mainly produce
choices: B Unfortified wines, often good value, outside the Douro’s Port zone
mcq.answer: B Unfortified wines, often good value, outside the Douro’s Port zone
mcq.why: Table-wine Portugal is much wider than Port; Lisboa and Alentejo lead volume.

mcq.q: Castelão is an important red grape in
choices: B Southern Portugal (for example Palmela), giving savoury, raspberry reds
mcq.answer: B Southern Portugal (for example Palmela), giving savoury, raspberry reds
mcq.why: Once the workhorse of the south; still seen in Lisboa and Península de Setúbal.

mcq.q: Paso Robles, compared with the Sonoma Coast, is generally
choices: B Warmer and better suited to Rhône varieties and ripe Cabernet
mcq.answer: B Warmer and better suited to Rhône varieties and ripe Cabernet
mcq.why: Inland San Luis Obispo heat; some west-side sites are more moderated.

mcq.q: Cafayate (Salta) is known for
choices: B High-altitude Torrontés, very aromatic and dry
mcq.answer: B High-altitude Torrontés, very aromatic and dry
mcq.why: Some of the world’s highest commercial vines; Torrontés is the white flagship.

mcq.q: Margaret River’s reputation rests on
choices: B Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay in a maritime south-west Australian climate
mcq.answer: B Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay in a maritime south-west Australian climate
mcq.why: Indian Ocean influence; structured Cabernet and high-quality Chardonnay.

mcq.q: Gisborne in New Zealand has been a historic centre for
choices: B Chardonnay (and some Gewurz) in a warmer, wetter east-coast setting
mcq.answer: B Chardonnay (and some Gewurz) in a warmer, wetter east-coast setting
mcq.why: Volume Chardonnay country; less famous now than Hawke’s Bay or Marlborough.

mcq.q: A PGI wine in the EU, compared with a PDO, usually has
choices: A Tighter yield and grape lists
B A larger area and more freedom, while still claiming a region
C No geographic name at all
mcq.answer: B A larger area and more freedom, while still claiming a region
mcq.why: Pays d’Oc, IGT Venezia Giulia, VdT Castilla are the idea.

mcq.q: Qualitätswein in Germany, unlike a Prädikat wine, may
choices: B Be chaptalised (where allowed) and is the broader PDO band below Prädikat
mcq.answer: B Be chaptalised (where allowed) and is the broader PDO band below Prädikat
mcq.why: Both are PDO; Prädikat forbids enrichment and is defined by must weight.

mcq.q: A US wine that names a county (for example Sonoma County) must contain at least
mcq.answer: A 75% from that county
mcq.why: County is 75%; AVA is 85%; state is 75% (with some state exceptions).

mcq.q: The Côte des Bar (Aube) is important in Champagne for
choices: B Pinot Noir from a slightly warmer, more southerly zone
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir from a slightly warmer, more southerly zone
mcq.why: Kim meridgian clay, a large share of Champagne’s Pinot, once undervalued.

mcq.q: Riddling (remuage) is the process of
choices: B Moving sediment into the neck before disgorgement
mcq.answer: B Moving sediment into the neck before disgorgement
mcq.why: Hand pupitre or gyropalette; then the neck is frozen and the plug ejected.

mcq.q: Prosecco Cartizze is
choices: B A small, prized hillside zone in Valdobbiadene
mcq.answer: B A small, prized hillside zone in Valdobbiadene
mcq.why: Superiore di Cartizze: a defined plot, usually a richer, often slightly sweeter style.

mcq.q: Crémant de Bourgogne is typically made from
choices: B Chardonnay and Pinot Noir (and allowed others) by the traditional method
mcq.answer: B Chardonnay and Pinot Noir (and allowed others) by the traditional method
mcq.why: Burgundy grapes, bottle ferment; a serious alternative to Champagne.

mcq.q: Demi-sec sparkling wine is best understood as
choices: D A synonym for Brut Nature
mcq.answer: B Noticeably sweet (about 32–50 g/L)
mcq.why: Match it to desserts or spicy-sweet food, not to bone-dry oysters.

mcq.q: Palo Cortado is a Sherry that
choices: A Stays under thick flor like Fino
B Behaves like an elegant, dry oxidative wine, between Amontillado and Oloroso in character
mcq.answer: B Behaves like an elegant, dry oxidative wine, between Amontillado and Oloroso in character
mcq.why: Rare; starts as if for Fino then loses flor and ages oxidatively.

mcq.q: Crusted Port is
choices: B A blend bottled with the intention that it will throw sediment, like a poor-man’s vintage
mcq.answer: B A blend bottled with the intention that it will throw sediment, like a poor-man’s vintage
mcq.why: Unfiltered, needs decanting; not necessarily a declared vintage year.

mcq.q: Bual (Boal) Madeira is
choices: B A medium-sweet style, darker and richer than Verdelho
mcq.answer: B A medium-sweet style, darker and richer than Verdelho
mcq.why: Sercial dry, Verdelho medium-dry, Bual medium-sweet, Malmsey sweet.

mcq.q: Maury, compared with Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, is usually
choices: B A Grenache-based VDN, often more oxidative or tawny in the traditional style
mcq.answer: B A Grenache-based VDN, often more oxidative or tawny in the traditional style
mcq.why: Roussillon Grenache; young vintage styles also exist (red fruit, less wood).

mcq.q: Montilla-Moriles makes wines in a Sherry spectrum, often from
choices: B Pedro Ximénez, and some unfortified because grapes reach high sugar
mcq.answer: B Pedro Ximénez, and some unfortified because grapes reach high sugar
mcq.why: Hot Andalusian plateau; PX is the star; some fino-style wines need little or no spirit.

mcq.q: Refermentation in bottle as a fault in a still wine shows as
choices: A A clean, designed sparkle with a dosage cork
B Unwanted haze, CO2 prickle and off-aromas in a wine meant to be still
C Only a buttery MLF note
mcq.answer: B Unwanted haze, CO2 prickle and off-aromas in a wine meant to be still
mcq.why: Residual sugar plus live yeast; the wine was not stable.

mcq.q: A young, very tannic red may be decanted in order to
choices: A Strip sediment that is not yet there and cool it to 4 °C
B Aerate it so the tannin and fruit open in the glass
mcq.answer: B Aerate it so the tannin and fruit open in the glass
mcq.why: Two reasons to decant: sediment (old wines) and aeration (young, closed wines).

mcq.q: Chilli heat in food is made more aggressive by wines that are
choices: A Slightly sweet and low in alcohol
B High in alcohol and tannin, and bone dry
mcq.answer: B High in alcohol and tannin, and bone dry
mcq.why: Alcohol burns; tannin plus capsaicin is harsh; a little sugar soothes.

mcq.q: On the SAT, colour intensity is recorded as
mcq.answer: B Pale, medium or deep
mcq.why: Appearance intensity is pale/medium/deep; aroma intensity uses the hyphenated five-term scale.

written.title: Question 1 — Germany: Mosel and Pfalz Riesling

parts.prompt: Compare climate, aspect and soil of the Mosel with the Pfalz, and the Riesling styles that result.
points: Mosel: cool continental, steep south-facing slate, river reflects light/heat; low alcohol, high acid, often some RS.
Pfalz: warmer, drier (Vosges/Haardt rain shadow), more sandstone/limestone, fuller, often dry (trocken) Riesling.
Both: Riesling holds acid; vintage and site matter.
Mosel Kabinett/Spätlese vs Pfalz Grosses Gewächs / trocken Spätlese.
Labour of steep vs tractor-friendly Pfalz.
Name a village each (e.g. Wehlen, Bernkastel vs Forst, Deidesheim) without inventing AOCs.

parts.prompt: Explain what a Prädikat tells you, and why a Spätlese can be either sweet or trocken.
points: Prädikat = minimum must weight at harvest, not bottled sweetness.
Order: Kabinett, Spätlese, Auslese, BA, Eiswein, TBA.
Ferment can be taken dry (trocken/halbtrocken) or stopped with RS (süssreserve or arrested ferment).
Chaptalisation is not allowed for Prädikat wines.
Label words trocken / feinherb / the Prädikat itself must be read together.
Quality still judged on balance, not sugar alone.

parts.prompt: Outline winery choices for a delicate Mosel Kabinett versus a dry Pfalz Grosses Gewächs-style Riesling.
points: Kabinett: early-ish pick, protective cool ferment, often residual sugar, low alcohol, stainless, no MLF, no new oak.
Dry GG: riper fruit, ferment dry, sometimes large old wood, lees for texture, still no new-barrique spice.
Both: variety and site in front; SO2 for cleanliness.
Sweet wines need stability (sterile filter or enough SO2).
Avoid carbonic banana notes.

parts.prompt: Outline the climates of Languedoc, Roussillon and Provence and name one still-wine AOC from each with its typical grapes.
points: All warm Mediterranean; Roussillon hotter and drier; Provence coastal with mistral; Languedoc more varied (hills vs coast).
Languedoc: Corbières, Minervois, Fitou, Saint-Chinian, Faugères — GSM + Carignan, Syrah; Picpoul de Pinet white.
Roussillon: Collioure (unfortified Grenache/Syrah/Mourvèdre) beside the VDNs.
Provence: Côtes de Provence rosé (Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah…); Bandol Mourvèdre.
IGP Pays d’Oc for variety-labelled volume.
Do not invent AOCs.

parts.prompt: Why has Carignan often been blended or old-vined rather than used as a young high-yield variety?
points: High yield on fertile plains gives rustic, high-acid, tannic, poorly ripe wine.
Old bush vines on poor hills give colour, spice and structure.
Carbonics can soften young Carignan for early drinking.
Blending with Grenache (fruit, alcohol) and Syrah (colour, perfume) is the Languedoc model.
EU vine-pull schemes removed much low-quality Carignan.
Award for naming a hill AOC where old Carignan still matters (Fitou, Corbières).

parts.prompt: Describe how a pale Provence rosé is usually made, and contrast it with a saignée Bandol or Tavel.
points: Provence: early pick for acid, direct press or very short maceration, cool stainless ferment, no oak, dry, pale.
Protective winemaking to keep a salmon/onion-skin colour and citrus/red-fruit notes.
Saignée: juice run off a red fermenter — deeper colour, more structure, a by-product of red wine.
Tavel: rosé-only, deliberately deeper and more structured.
Bandol rosé: Mourvèdre in the blend, more body, can take a little texture.
None of these are sweet White Zinfandel-style wines in the WSET picture.

parts.prompt: Describe how Asti and Moscato d’Asti are made and how they differ in pressure, alcohol and sweetness.
points: Grape: Moscato Bianco (Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains) in Piedmont.
Tank method: ferment under pressure; stop by chilling and filtering to keep sugar and aroma.
Asti: fully sparkling (spumante), about 7–9.5% abv, sweet.
Moscato d’Asti: frizzante, lower pressure, often about 4.5–6.5% abv, sweet, very grapey.
No traditional-method autolysis; drink young.
Contrast with dry Alsace Muscat and with Champagne.

parts.prompt: Why is a long lees ageing in bottle the wrong tool for this grape?
points: Muscat’s point is primary grape, orange blossom and musk.
Autolysis adds biscuit/toast that hides those notes.
Low alcohol and residual sugar are part of the style; a complete dry bottle ferment would change the wine.
Cost and time would not match an early-drinking sweet wine.
Tank is fast, aromatic and cheap enough for the market.

parts.prompt: Give service and pairing notes for Moscato d’Asti, including one dish to avoid.
points: Serve very well chilled; drink from a youthful bottling.
Light cakes, fruit, wedding cake, lightly spicy fruit dishes; or as a low-alcohol aperitif.
Avoid: dry, tannic red-wine food (steak), or a dish sweeter than the wine.
Opened bottle: fridge, a day or two; it goes flat and tired.
Do not decant.
Glass: white-wine glass is fine; not a tiny sticky glass only.

parts.prompt: Describe Madeira’s climate and the four classic grape styles from driest to sweetest.
points: Warm Atlantic island; mountains, so sites vary; historically a shipping wine that heated at sea.
Sercial: dry, high acid, citrus/almond.
Verdelho: medium-dry, smoky citrus.
Bual/Boal: medium-sweet, raisin and caramel.
Malmsey/Malvasia: sweetest, rich brown sugar and toffee.
Tinta Negra is the workhorse for many blended/younger wines.
Acidity is high in all styles — that is why they last.
Estufagem: stainless or vats heated (about 45–50 °C) for months; used for inexpensive 3-year wines; can give a baked note if crude.
Canteiro: casks in warm lofts, years of gentle heat and oxidation; quality 5-year to vintage/colheita.
Both create the cooked, nutty, stable character; canteiro is more complex.
Fortification timing differs by intended sweetness (earlier = sweeter).
Once matured this way, Madeira is almost indestructible.
Award for mentioning frasqueira / vintage long canteiro.

parts.prompt: Give storage, service and pairing advice for a 10-year Malmsey and a dry Sercial.
points: Both: store upright once for service; they last weeks or months after opening.
Sercial: lightly chilled, aperitif, with consommé or olives.
Malmsey: slightly cool, not cold; chocolate, rich cake, blue cheese.
No need to decant for sediment (unlike Vintage Port).
Do not treat an open Madeira as fragile Fino.
Match sweetness: Sercial with savoury, Malmsey with sweet.
